transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair, Marcus Hale, Leah Kim
Recording ID: ff-20270803-mirahealth-001

Summary (auto):
- Purpose: scope a 6-week POC to evaluate open models for multi-domain extraction (radiology notes + intake forms) with multilingual support (EN/ES).
- Primary success criteria: entity extraction F1 >= 0.85 on clinical entities; latency p95 < 350ms for 8k context workload; cost target < $0.002/token equivalent on average.
- Model shortlist discussed: Llama-3-70B (quant), Mistral-Refine, OpenAssistant fine-tuned variant, and a smaller per-domain finetune candidate (13B).
- Next: Redwood to provide benchmark matrix and run initial throughput bench; customer to provide sample data; schedule latency deep-dive and security review.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria definition and thresholding
- Workload sizing (daily tokens, concurrency, typical sequence lengths)
- Benchmarks (quality metrics, latency, cost)
- Model shortlist & quality tradeoffs (multilang, domain sensitivity)
- Timeline and next milestones

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, today is to align on the POC scope. Connor and I will run through the shortlist and the bench plan. Who do we have from MiraHealth?
[00:12] Priya: Hi this is Priya, uh Head of AI. Marcus is on for platform questions and Leah will cover the clinical examples.
[00:18] Marcus: Yep hi, Marcus here.
[00:20] Leah: Hey all.
[00:22] Sofia: Awesome. Quick housekeeping, we'll record, we'll share notes, and Connor will circulate the benchmark template after. Any constraints up front? SLOs, regs?
[00:31] Priya: Main constraint is PHI handling — most data will be pseudonymized but we still need audit logs and K-M-S backed encryption; also EU residency for a subset. We also do have a latency expectation, like sub 300 to 400 ms p95 for our ingestion path otherwise UX breaks.
[00:46] Connor: Got it. For clarity, are you measuring p95 end-to-end from the app or just inference? That changes the numbers a bit.
[00:53] Priya: Prefer end-to-end, because front-end timeout is what we care about. But we'll record both if possible.
[00:58] Sofia: OK noted. Quick intro from us: Redwood can run hosted or dedicated, or private in a V-P-C — apologies if the transcript picks that up weirdly — and we have built-in rollbacks and prefix cache to lower token costs.
[01:12] Leah: When you say prefix cache, how's that behave with per-patient contexts where history differs a lot?
[01:19] Connor: It's a workload-dependent thing. If you have stable prompt scaffolding we can get big gains. For variable patient notes it's less, but KV cache still helps for long chart contexts.
[01:29] Priya: Cool. Moving to success criteria: Our product team wants two buckets — quality and infra. Quality: entity extraction (ICD codes, med names, dosages) F1 target 0.85 +/-; hallucination rate low, which we'll measure via manual spot checks. Infra: p95 latency under 350ms and endpoint availability 99.9.
[01:47] Sofia: Great, that's specific. For the POC we'd propose defining a golden set of 500 annotated notes across the two domains — radiology and intake forms — and reserve 100 as blind test. Does that sound doable?
[01:58] Leah: Yes, we can redact and prepare that. We'll need instructions on formatting.
[02:03] Marcus: On sizing, current volume: ~1.2M requests/month, average tokenizes per request around 400 tokens, peak concurrency ~25 rps in US region. For POC, we want to simulate 30 rps to include burst headroom.
[02:18] Connor: OK so ballpark tokens/day ~ 16M. That informs batching profiles and which model families are economical.
[02:25] Priya: Also multilingual need — Spanish primarily, maybe Portuguese for certain clinics. How are you thinking of handling that in the shortlist?
[02:34] Sofia: We suggested a mixed shortlist: a high-capacity 70B variant for quality (Llama-3-70B-q4 or similar), a mid-sized 13–16B model with strong multilingual properties, and an instruction-tuned Mistral-refine style for cheaper throughput. We also included an OpenAssistant-based fine-tune of your domain for a final stage.
[02:52] Priya: Any concerns around hallucination with the larger models? Historically bigger models can produce more confident but incorrect entities.
[02:59] Connor: Right, hallucination assessment will be in the bench. We'll use both automated entity precision/recall metrics and curated manual review. We also can add hard constraints in the prompt to reduce freeform answers.
[03:11] [small crosstalk] Marcus: Cost-wise what's the delta between 70B quant and 13B?
[03:15] Connor: Very roughly 3–4x compute cost on similar hardware. But once quantized and with batch/kv caching the effective token cost narrows in many workloads. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:26] Sofia: For the POC plan, we propose a 6-week timeline: week 0 (prep) — dataset + infra access; week 1–2 — baseline model runs and latency/throughput bench; week 3–4 — model finetuning/adapter experiments and multilingual checks; week 5 — blind test on golden set; week 6 — wrap + decision.
[03:45] Leah: That sounds good. We might need a longer finetune window if results look close.
[03:50] Priya: Agreed. Also security review ideally in parallel — Marcus will coordinate.
[03:55] Marcus: Yep. We'll need your SOC2 summary, and a quick run of private deployment options; on-prem could be hard but VPC with customer-managed K-M-S is doable.
[04:05] Sofia: We'll share our SOC2 summary and an RSA-style checklist — and Connor will follow up on private deployment notes.
[04:12] [00:04:12 timestamp typo in auto]
[04:15] Connor: On benchmarks — we recommend three passes: quality (entity F1, extraction exact match), latency (p50,p95,p99 inference-only and end-to-end), and cost (tokens/sec and $/effective-token). We also recommend a robustness suite: swapped names, abbreviations, misspellings common in clinical notes.
[04:32] Priya: Are you able to bench multilingual on the same model or do we need separate runs?
[04:38] Connor: Same model but separate test sets — Spanish/Portuguese test sets. For some models the drop is significant, so we'll flag that.
[04:46] Leah: For entity mapping, we need a post-processing layer that normalizes med names to our internal dictionary. Is that part of the POC?
[04:54] Sofia: We can include a simple normalization pass in the pipeline for evaluation. If you have the dictionary, we can plug it in.
[04:59] Marcus: Regarding throughput: our integration is via a serverless ingestion layer. If you recommend batching, we need details on buffer windows — can't add latency more than 50ms.
[05:09] Connor: We will present a few batching configurations; continuous batching can be tuned to maintain tight latency SLOs. For your p95 goal we'd likely keep small batch sizes and more aggressive autoscaling.
[05:20] Priya: Ok, model shortlist specifics — can you enumerate candidate models and why each was chosen?
[05:26] Connor: Sure. Candidate 1: Llama-3-70B-quant — best raw quality for complex context, good for radiology interpretation where nuance matters. Candidate 2: Mistral-refine type model (70B-ish or instruction-tuned variant) — strong instruction following, good balance for extraction tasks. Candidate 3: 13B multilingual family (e.g., ?13B-multi) — lower cost, strong Spanish performance, good for intake forms. Candidate 4: OpenAssistant-domain-tune — small adapter/fine-tune on your annotated set, intended to punch above its size on domain-specific entities.
[06:00] Priya: Any concerns about inference infra — memory and VRAM fitting?
[06:04] Connor: Yes for 70B we need multi-GPU or quantized single-GPU depending on hardware. We'll run automatic kernel selection and recommend either dedicated GPU pools or Redwood dedicated nodes in the POC. We'll note which ones fit on 80GB A100 vs 48GB hardware.
[06:20] Marcus: We use a mix of NVMe ephemeral storage and S3; any recommendation for kv cache persistence?
[06:28] Connor: KV cache is in-memory during inference; for warm-starts we can snapshot. For your workload it's less necessary unless you do very long multi-turn histories.
[06:37] Leah: For evaluation metrics: aside from F1 what about clinical correctness? Something like severity detection or incorrect med warnings?
[06:46] Sofia: We can add a clinical-error metric: count of medically-significant hallucinations flagged by your clinicians in the blind test. That will be part of the manual review.
[06:55] Priya: Good. On timeline logistics: once you share the bench template we'll fill sample dataset by Friday. Then first-run benches by week 2, and we reconvene after that.
[07:05] Sofia: Perfect. We'll also put together a candidate cost model with per-token estimates.
[07:09] Marcus: Is there precedent for using smaller models for first pass extraction then heavier model for verification?
[07:15] Connor: Yes, a cascade approach — cheaper model extracts candidates then a bigger model verifies or normalizes. That often reduces cost while preserving quality. We'll include that as an optional path.
[07:25] Leah: How do you handle PII/PHI during model eval? We can't have raw PHI leave our environment.
[07:31] Sofia: For POC we recommend redacted or tokenized sets. If needed we can bring a private deployment to your VPC or run on-prem. Marcus, you'll coordinate which option.
[07:40] Marcus: We'll try S3 staging with strict IAM and VPC endpoints first.
[07:44] Priya: A couple of small questions: 1) can you measure hallucination rate automatically? 2) what about model drift monitoring after POC?
[07:53] Connor: 1) We can approximate hallucination with heuristics and QA tests but manual review is still required for clinical risk. 2) Post-POC, Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — we can demo that in the console.
[08:07] Sofia: Ok recap: deliverables = benchmark matrix + model shortlist (Connor), SOC2 + security summary (Sofia), S3 staging details (Marcus), annotated golden set (customer). Meet again after baseline bench (TBD week 2).
[08:21] Priya: Sounds good. Additional risk: if costs exceed projections we may need a cutoff in week 3.
[08:27] Sofia: We'll include cost caps in the bench and show tradeoffs.
[08:30] [longer pause as attendees review notes]
[08:45] Connor: One more note on multilingual — some models tag code-switching poorly; we'll create a mixed-language shard in the test set to simulate clinic notes.
[08:55] Leah: Great, that's realistic.
[08:58] Marcus: For the technical deep-dive, we want to cover VPC peering, ingress egress, and K-M-S integration. Can we do a 60min follow-up?
[09:06] Sofia: Yes we'll schedule a dedicated technical session — Connor and our infra engineer will join. How's Aug 9th at 10am PT?
[09:14] Marcus: Works for me.
[09:16] Priya: Works.
[09:17] Sofia: Ok, I'll send calendar invite. Any final questions?
[09:22] Priya: None from me. Thanks everyone.
[09:25] Sofia: Thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and links.
